en.fundamental: Constellation Energy sits at the bottleneck of the AI power value chain as the largest US nuclear operator, expanded in January 2026 via its Calpine gas and geothermal acquisition. On November 9, 2026, CEG posted Q3 adjusted operating earnings of USD 5.06 per share (up 66% from USD 3.04) and GAAP EPS of USD 5.19 on USD 9.55 billion in revenue, lifted by higher PJM capacity prices, Calpine accretion, and a 97.2% nuclear capacity factor. Management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to USD 12.50–12.80 (from USD 11.50–12.50), placing shares near 20x guided earnings. Growth visibility widened through the October 27 conditional USD 5 billion DOE uprate loan, the Peak+ hybrid product (270 MW initial contract), and a USD 715 million agreement for the 609 MW Rhode Island State Energy Center.
en.headline: Bearish chart clashes with Q3 earnings beat, raised guidance, and $5B DOE loan
news: November 19–23, 2026: CEG slid to USD 237.41 on November 20 amid a broad AI-tech selloff and a November 19 push by seven state ratepayer advocates and PJM's market monitor to delay December's 2029/30 capacity auction, before rebounding 6.03% to USD 251.72 on November 23.

November 19, 2026: Barclays reiterated an Overweight rating and lifted its CEG price target from USD 345 to USD 371 following Q3 results, joining Morgan Stanley (Overweight, USD 393) and BMO Capital (Outperform, USD 335) in raising post-earnings targets.

November 9, 2026: Constellation reported Q3 adjusted EPS of USD 5.06 (vs. USD 3.04 a year earlier) on USD 9.55 billion in revenue, raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to USD 12.50–12.80, and launched Peak+ with a 20-year, 270 MW contract.
October 30, 2026: The board declared a quarterly dividend of USD 0.4265 per share, payable December 4, 2026 to shareholders of record on November 16.

October 27, 2026: The U.S. Department of Energy announced a conditional loan commitment of up to USD 5 billion under Project UPRISE to fund nearly 1.1 GW of nuclear uprates across eight Constellation plants in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania—complementing Google's October 6 deal for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity.
en.opportunity: For long-term AI-infrastructure investors, the 33.9% pullback from CEG's 52-week high has compressed valuation to roughly 20x raised 2026 guidance (USD 12.50–12.80) even as earnings visibility improves. Unlike speculative power plays, Constellation is adding roughly 1.1 GW of carbon-free capacity via existing-plant uprates backed by 20-year hyperscaler PPAs with Google and Amazon plus a conditional USD 5 billion DOE loan that lowers financing costs. Technically, high-volume buying near the USD 236.25 lower Bollinger Band and USD 228.63 52-week low marks a clear support zone to monitor for base-building.
en.opportunityCheck: The page's sub-scores for market position and bottleneck pricing power look well calibrated given CEG's unmatched US nuclear fleet and tight PJM supply. However, the AI revenue exposure score looks too low and should move higher. Across its Q3 2026 update on November 9, CEG detailed 20-year hyperscaler agreements with Google (890 MW uprates plus 2,700 MW supply) and Amazon (690 MW), a 270 MW Peak+ deal, and Calpine's data-center power footprint. Optionality also improves with the October 27 conditional USD 5 billion DOE loan, though PJM ratepayer pushback caps unlimited pricing upside.
pros: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS jumped 66% year-over-year to USD 5.06 on November 9, prompting a full-year guidance hike to USD 12.50–12.80.
A conditional USD 5 billion DOE loan announced on October 27 lowers financing costs for roughly 1.1 GW of nuclear uprates across eight plants.
Long-term hyperscaler contracts—including Google's 890 MW deal (October 6), Amazon's 690 MW Calvert Cliffs deal, and a 270 MW Peak+ agreement—lock in 20-year revenue.
Nuclear fleet reliability reached a 97.2% Q3 capacity factor (99.2% in peak summer), reinforcing CEG's 24/7 baseload advantage.
risks: Regulatory and capacity-market risk: PJM ratepayer advocates and Monitoring Analytics pushing to delay December 2026's capacity auction or tighten price caps could trim merchant capacity margins.
Financing and execution risk: The USD 5 billion DOE loan is conditional on due diligence, and multi-year nuclear uprates across eight plants (through 2032) risk delays or cost inflation.
AI capex sentiment and valuation volatility: CEG trades as a high-beta proxy for AI data-center spending, making shares vulnerable to broader tech drawdowns.
Operational and integration risk: Unplanned nuclear outages or slower synergies from the Calpine and Rhode Island gas plant acquisitions could weigh on cash flow.
en.summary: Constellation Energy (CEG) trades at USD 251.72 as of November 23, 2026, down 33.9% from its 52-week high of USD 380.78 despite a 6.03% single-day bounce. Technicals remain bearish below all major moving averages, weighed down by November's AI-sector selloff and PJM capacity-auction pushback. Fundamentally, the nuclear moat is intact: on November 9, CEG beat Q3 estimates with USD 5.06 adjusted EPS, raised 2026 guidance to USD 12.50–12.80, launched its Peak+ hybrid power product, and followed an October 27 conditional USD 5 billion DOE loan for 1.1 GW of nuclear uprates.
en.technical: CEG's technical posture as of November 23, 2026 is bearish despite a sharp single-day rebound of 6.03% to USD 251.72. The trend structure is weak: price trades below all three exponential moving averages (EMAs, which smooth price to show trend)—EMA 50 at USD 265.91, EMA 100 at USD 269.98, and EMA 200 at USD 278.29—and those lines are stacked in bearish order with shorter averages beneath longer ones. Momentum also leans negative. MACD (a trend-momentum gauge comparing two moving averages) sits at -3.25, below its -1.39 signal line with a -1.87 histogram, showing sellers still hold control. RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge where under 30 is oversold) stands at 44.85—weak, though not deeply oversold. Within its Bollinger Bands (a volatility envelope around the 20-day average spanning USD 236.25 to USD 286.85), price sits in the lower half below the USD 261.55 midpoint and rests in the bottom 15% of its 52-week range (USD 228.63–380.78). Volume of 5.20 million shares ran 29% above the 20-day average of 4.03 million, confirming dip-buying interest near USD 236 support, though closing below the USD 255.24 open leaves immediate resistance at USD 261.55–265.91.

th.technical: ภาพรวมเทคนิคของ CEG ณ วันที่ 23 พฤศจิกายน 2026 ยังอยู่ในฝั่งขาลง (bearish) แม้ราคาจะดีดแรง 6.03% มาปิดที่ USD 251.72 โครงสร้างแนวโน้มยังอ่อนแอ โดยราคาต่ำกว่าเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยเคลื่อนที่แบบเอ็กซ์โปเนนเชียล (EMA ซึ่งใช้กรองความผันผวนเพื่อดูแนวโน้ม) ทั้งสามเส้น ได้แก่ EMA 50 ที่ USD 265.91, EMA 100 ที่ USD 269.98 และ EMA 200 ที่ USD 278.29 ซึ่งเรียงตัวแบบขาลงเต็มรูปแบบ ด้านโมเมนตัมยังเป็นลบ โดย MACD (ตัวชี้วัดแรงส่งแนวโน้มจากการเทียบเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยสองเส้น) อยู่ที่ -3.25 ต่ำกว่าเส้น Signal (-1.39) พร้อมแท่งฮิสโตแกรมติดลบ -1.87 สะท้อนแรงขายยังคุมเกม ขณะที่ RSI 14 (มาตรวัดแรงซื้อขาย 0–100 หากต่ำกว่า 30 คือขายมากเกินไป) อยู่ที่ 44.85 ถือว่าอ่อนแรงแต่ยังไม่เข้าเขต oversold เมื่อเทียบกับ Bollinger Bands (กรอบความผันผวนรอบค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วันช่วง USD 236.25–286.85) ราคาอยู่ครึ่งล่างใต้เส้นกลาง USD 261.55 และอยู่ช่วงล่าง 15% ของกรอบรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ (USD 228.63–380.78) อย่างไรก็ดี ปริมาณซื้อขาย 5.20 ล้านหุ้น สูงกว่าค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วัน (4.03 ล้านหุ้น) ราว 29% ยืนยันแรงรับใกล้แนวรับ USD 236 แต่การปิดต่ำกว่าราคาเปิด USD 255.24 ทิ้งแนวต้านระยะใกล้ไว้ที่ USD 261.55–265.91
